subject: Polity
description: Articles 5-11, Citizenship Act 1955, voting age, NRIs

questions.stem: The concept of SINGLE CITIZENSHIP in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
questions.explanation: Single citizenship — from the British Constitution. (USA and most federal countries have dual citizenship — state + federal.) In India, regardless of state of residence, every citizen has the same Indian citizenship. Articles 5-11 of Part II cover citizenship.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Citizenship Act, 1955 lists how many modes of acquiring Indian citizenship?
questions.explanation: 5 modes: (1) by birth, (2) by descent, (3) by registration, (4) by naturalisation, (5) by incorporation of territory. Termination: renunciation, termination (when acquires foreign citizenship), deprivation.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The VOTING AGE in India was reduced from 21 to 18 by which amendment?
questions.explanation: 61st Amendment, 1988 (took effect 1989). Article 326 modified: minimum voting age 18 instead of 21. Rajiv Gandhi government. 18 ECI's 2024 general election added ~97 crore voters total.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: OVERSEAS CITIZEN OF INDIA (OCI) card holders:

options.option_text: Are Indian citizens with full voting rights
Are foreign citizens with multi-entry multi-purpose lifelong visa; cannot vote
Must give up their foreign citizenship within 5 years

questions.explanation: OCI — introduced 2005, merges with PIO from 2015. Foreign citizens (except from Pakistan / Bangladesh) of Indian origin get: lifelong visa, parity in most matters except voting / elected office / agricultural land / government employment.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The ECI conducts elections under which constitutional Article?
questions.explanation: Article 324 — vests the 'superintendence, direction, and control' of elections to Parliament, state legislatures, President, and VP in the Election Commission of India. Set up 25 January 1950 (a day before the Constitution took effect) — 25 January is now National Voters' Day.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The CAA (Citizenship Amendment Act) was passed in:
questions.explanation: Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 — provides a path to Indian citizenship for non-Muslim religious minorities (Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, Christian) who entered India from Pakistan, Bangladesh, or Afghanistan by 31 December 2014. Rules notified 11 March 2024. Nationwide protests and legal challenges followed the 2019 Act.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Consider the following about ANTI-DEFECTION LAW. 1. Added via the 52nd Amendment, 1985 (10th Schedule). 2. Disqualifies an elected MP/MLA who voluntarily gives up party membership or votes against party whip. 3. A split (one-third) or merger (two-third) of party legislators can escape disqualification; BUT the 91st Amendment (2003) removed the 'split' exception. 4. The Speaker/Chairperson is the ADJUDICATING authority. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. The 52nd Amendment (Rajiv Gandhi's tenure) introduced the 10th Schedule. The 91st Amendment (2003) tightened the law by removing the 'split' safe harbour — now only a two-third 'merger' is allowed.
